Hello, I'm Subarukayak and I too am a reddit refugee. Ask me anything you like.

I first joined reddit in the early 2000s. I'd probably spent well over $5k on the site and site related activities (donation, various charities, pizza, SecretSanta, et al). To add to that, I did a whole lot of artwork for the site in making custom Snoos for various things. If you 404 a reddit page and see the little confused Snoo... that is me.

http://subarukayak.imgur.com/all/

http://www.redditblog.com/2010/05/reddits-may-2010-state-of-servers.html

Hell, Alexis tweeted over this one... http://i.imgur.com/EjD0h.jpg

I am the artist that created the revised 404s and the little "You Broke Reddit" pics. I also did a bit of work for sales and such for E3. I was an active participant on several of the art related subs. I helped a little with art bits in getting the Secret Santa bits off the ground the first time around. That's just the big bits I can remember right off... oh, and /r/fffffffuuuuuuuuuuu was partly my fault. And some of the adverts for radioreddit.

The bits of 'making things better for everyone else' resonated with me. I was involved with reddit because I liked the community and felt connected to something far more powerful than myself. For Donor's choose I bought a $2k telescope for middle school kids in Oakland. I've picked up local redditors in Dallas and gave them rides to the airport, volunteered for various disasters championed by the reddit community.

I think I just broke my arm patting myself on the back... to be short- I liked the old reddit. It was my online home for almost a decade. I didn't leave reddit all 'willy nilly' in a huff. It's been a long time coming. I am less relieved and more disappointed.

More on this later.

Welcome! Your work is incredible and I am excited to see how you can help voat! I share your feeling of disappointment, but I think it's sort of misplaced for me: the community is what matters. The domain is arbitrary. Sure, reddit had some good moments, but hell, so did MySpace, DIGG or AOL. In the end, the freedom of ideas is what matters, and that's why we're here.

I never made it to Digg. Reddit for me was like TotalFark but hundreds of pages deep and didn't cost anything. I still hop back to Fark once in a while just to see the Photoshop threads and to check for Florida tags. I think I blocked out the AOL experience entirely though I have memories of stringing together little scripts and using it as an email bomb... Reruns of 'All in the Family' and 'CHiPs' before switching over to the Headbanger's Ball. I've always been more Iron Maiden than Sabbath although today it's KMFDM and Die Antwoord.

This whole leap from Reddit is somewhat surreal. I dumped a lot of history. Attacking the freedom of ideas is only one little piece of a long line of things reddit engaged in. I didn't agree with how they handled the Violentacres fiasco. The emergence of SRS/SRD didn't affect me much- I don't think I ever made it on their radar... don't get me wrong, they're a cancer- just as Tumblerinas and HAES is a cancer- and they're killing reddit if they haven't already.

Everyday on reddit is a pro-military pic/story/circlejerk. 90% of the frontpage is facebook garbage. MFW, MRW, DAE, all of that shit is what killed reddit for me. Unoriginal rehashed mass produced souless content parroted to the forefront and paraded as if it's some grand accomplishment. Compound that with the shit /r/news was doing and the emergence of the automod and entire domains getting axed- steering the content in spite of what the votes say- I was just loitering there waiting for a catalyst to kick in.

There's still small holdouts of community left on reddit. They don't stay long but it wasn't uncommon to see a good cause pop up. It seems it devolved into a market minded force where a movement isn't allowed to root like it use to. Reddit use to sit on a subject till it was beaten to death- now an idea comes along and before it can be tasted a newer idea is already coming down the pipe. I think the user base was fragmented deliberately. The 500k+ rally on the Grand Mall in DC scared some folks. The email campaigns that put Gawker Media in the poorhouse were swiftly neutered by Admin (Kotaku/gamergate). Reddit meet-ups are without purpose beyond themselves.

Like I said, it was a long time coming. I feel for anyone who has real money tied to it.
